Subject: Dataflow visual + access ownership for PII (HealthSync)

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for walking through the onboarding checklist yesterday. As part of our internal privacy review we need: 1) an updated dataflow visualization that highlights where HealthSync PII (patient_id, dob, treatment_codes) enters Redwood; 2) a clear ownership map detailing which Redwood teams/roles have access to live request data, logs, and backups; and 3) a current list of subprocessors involved in any cross-border transfers.

Specific asks: 
- Annotated diagram (PNG/SVG) that labels ingress points, transient caches (KV cache), and long-term storage buckets.
- A per-bucket retention bucket name + legal basis (if applicable).
- Who holds the KMS keys (Redwood-managed vs. customer BYOK) and where audit logs live.
- Evidence we can include in our SOC scope: sample exchange of an anonymized request + SFTP transfer logs or signed subprocessor agreements.

Can you get this over by EOD Friday (Aug 14)? We may need to share it with our privacy office. If you prefer a quick 30-min call to walk through, tell me which slots you have.

Cheers,
Sam
Sam Patel
Head of Security & Privacy
HealthSync

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>

Hi Sam — thanks for the clear list. Attaching an initial pass (redwood_dataflow_v1.png) and an access owner matrix (access_matrix_owners.csv). Below is a short explainer and next steps.

What I attached:
- redwood_dataflow_v1.png (initial annotated diagram) — highlights ingress, inference runtime (KV cache highlighted), short-lived logs, and encrypted backup buckets.
- access_matrix_owners.csv — rows for each data store + columns for read/write/admin owners by role.

Short answers to your bullets:
- Retention buckets: we call them TTL-1d (24h transient), TTL-30d (ephemeral logs for debugging), and TTL-730d (backups for compliance). See access_matrix_owners.csv for owner and retention justification.
- KMS: For hosted accounts we use Redwood-managed KMS with customer BYOK available for Dedicated/Private. I note this in the subprocessors doc. Audit logs are stored in an append-only system (separate logging cluster) and we can provide time-limited exports.
- Evidence: I included a sanitized sample request (anonymized) and a checklist of logs we can export; SFTP transfer logs are available on request — need to know the date range you want.

For the cross-border subprocessor list I have a draft (subprocessors_list_20260811.pdf) but need compliance to confirm the latest commercial terms for a couple of EU partner caches. Looping in Mina and Kimberly to confirm details and finalize by Friday.

Next steps: 
- Mina: please confirm which internal roles have Admin access to the backup bucket and whether we can pull last-30-day SFTP transfer logs for an exemplar timeframe (Aug 1–7).
- Kimberly: can you review the retention justifications and mark any PII fields that should be redacted from the diagram before we share externally?
- Sam: if you can confirm the exact fields you want highlighted (patient_id, ssn, treatment_code, dob), we will mark them.

Irene Choi
Senior Privacy Program Manager
Redwood Inference
